etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tasten, borrowed from Old French taster, from assumed Vulgar Latin *tastāre, from assumed Vulgar Latin *taxitāre, a new iterative of Latin taxāre (“to touch sharply”), from tangere (“to touch”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂g-. Almost displaced native Middle English smaken, smakien (“to taste”) (from Old English smacian (“to taste”)), Middle English smecchen (“to taste, smack”) (from Old English smæċċan (“to taste”)) (whence Modern English smack), Middle English buriȝen (“to taste”) (from Old English byrigan, birian (“to taste”)).

definitions.definition: One of the sensations produced by the tongue in response to certain chemicals; the quality of giving this sensation.
The sense that consists in the perception and interpretation of this sensation.
A small sample of food, drink, or recreational drugs.
(countable and uncountable) A person's implicit set of preferences, especially esthetic, though also culinary, sartorial, etc.

quote.citation: 1777, Richard Brinsley Sheridan, The School for Scandal, II.i:
quote.text: That's very true indeed Sir Peter! after having married you I should never pretend to Taste again I allow.

quote.citation: 1907 August, Robert W[illiam] Chambers, chapter VIII, in The Younger Set, New York, N.Y.: D. Appleton & Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: "My tastes," he said, still smiling, "incline me to the garishly sunlit side of this planet." And, to tease her and arouse her to combat: "I prefer a farandole to a nocturne; I'd rather have a painting than an etching; Mr. Whistler bores me with his monochromatic mud; I don't like dull colours, dull sounds, dull intellects; […]."

quote.citation: 1963, Margery Allingham, chapter 1, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:
quote.text: The huge square box, parquet-floored and high-ceilinged, had been arranged to display a suite of bedroom furniture designed and made in the halcyon days of the last quarter of the nineteenth century, when modish taste was just due to go clean out of fashion for the best part of the next hundred years.

definitions.definition: (figuratively) A small amount of experience with something that gives a sense of its quality as a whole.

quote.citation: 2007, KT Tunstall (lyrics and music), “Saving My Face”, in Drastic Fantastic‎[1]:
quote.text: I'm all out of luck / I'm all out of faith / I would give everything just for one taste / But everything's here, all out of place […]

definitions.definition: A kind of narrow and thin silk ribbon.
(transitive) To sample the flavor of something orally.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, copulative) To have a taste; to excite a particular sensation by which flavor is distinguished.
(transitive) To identify (a flavor) by sampling something orally.
